Overview and relationship to the market

Softmax Offset is a 5-member bagged ensemble and the production model a live staking decision would use. Every figure below is read from a declared artifact: this report fits nothing, loads no booster, recomputes no prediction and calls no betting optimiser.

Softmax Offset is better than the market by 0.004777 race_multinomial_log_loss on the evaluated races. The direction holds in every one of the 11 evaluated years.

How each evaluation year was fitted

The 2016 evaluation model was trained on the initial 2010-2015 set. Each later evaluation adds the preceding complete season, so the training window expands by one year; the 2026 model uses 2010-2025. Every evaluation year is fitted separately -- 11 fits in all -- and no evaluation year's outcomes appear in its own fit.

Deltas in this report use model_minus_market_log_loss: race_multinomial_log_loss, where negative is better. That is stated because three delta fields existed in this repository and they did not all point the same way.

Similarity is not accuracy

Similarity is not accuracy. Correlation, rank agreement, top-choice agreement, probability mass moved, divergence and entropy describe how the model relates to the market; paired race log-loss says which probabilities better described the recorded winners.

What this report covers

Every metric here is reported beside the market's own implied probabilities on the same races, normalised within each race. The delta is this model's race log loss minus the market's on the same races.

Every figure in this report covers the evaluation window beginning in 2016. 2015 is earlier than the window and is excluded from every evaluation figure below, including the bankroll paths. The feature-effect grid is the one exception, and says so where it appears: a learned response direction is a property of each year's fit rather than of the evaluation population.

Splits present: test, train_apparent, train_prequential. Only the forward test split is scored above. The others exist to be compared against it -- an apparent-fit number looks far better than a forward one -- and are never pooled with it.

Out-of-fold margin sources: market_fallback, model.

How often this model's first pick differs from the market's, and whether it is right when it does. Disagreeing more is not better on its own -- the useful figure is the win rate conditional on disagreeing, because a model that disagrees often and loses is worse than one that never disagrees. The last column is how often the seeds pick the same runner as each other, which bounds how much of any disagreement is signal rather than seed noise.

Calibration

Reliability by pipeline stage, on bins fixed across the whole report so two stages are comparable, pooled from the per-year counts rather than averaged over years. Stages: market, raw_offset, temperature, market_blend, bagged.

The largest departure is the 0.000 to 0.010 bin, and every stage misses there: market 0.54, raw_offset 0.80, temperature 0.87, market_blend 0.74, bagged 0.72. market is furthest from 1.0 at 0.54, meaning that bin won fewer races than it priced; temperature is closest at 0.87, so this bin is where the pipeline moves calibration most. On the market stage that bin holds 11,383 runners, the 6th smallest of 10 bins, so the departure is not a thin-bin artefact. Calibration in this bin does not improve monotonically through the pipeline: temperature reaches 0.87 and market_blend falls back to 0.74, so that step gives back part of the correction rather than adding to it.

Model diagnostics

Ensemble stability

Runners covered
101,810
Years
11
Seeds bagged
5

Member dispersion per runner. The bag is only worth its cost if members genuinely disagree: an ensemble whose members agree everywhere is one fit with five times the runtime. The per-runner spread across members is in ensemble_diagnostics.parquet, race by race.

Feature and correction effects

These are corrections, not drivers of winning

The booster learns a correction to log(Implied_Prob), so a feature's attributed effect is its disagreement with the market -- not its contribution to a horse winning. Read the naive way, the sign inverts.

Metric definitions
Supported years
Years in which the response was materially distinguishable from zero; for race-constant features, years whose magnitude changed across the feature range.
Yearly direction agreement
Share of annual response-curve bins whose sign matches that bin's dominant sign. 100% means every year's curve points the same way.
Importance-rank stability
How little the feature's magnitude rank moves between years. 100% means no rank movement.
Seed variation relative to effect
Seed-to-seed spread divided by the feature's average effect size. Lower is better.
Input drift (PSI)
Distribution shift from the first to latest evaluation year. Zero means no measured shift; above 0.25 is substantial.
Type
CONT is continuous; CAT is categorical or binary.

32 features in the artifact; the 30 with the largest mean absolute attributed effect are shown. The rest are in feature_stability.csv -- the table is truncated, not the evidence.

This grid covers every year the run fitted, including any the evaluation population excludes. A learned response direction is a property of that year's fit rather than of the race population the headline metrics are computed on, and its per-feature mean is the stability table's tail_effect exactly -- so restricting one and not the other would have two parts of this report describe different populations. 18 of 32 features keep the same sign in every year they appear in. For the seven features that are constant within a race -- a racecourse, a surface -- the cell is the correction's magnitude and not its direction, because a race-constant feature cancels from every pairwise utility difference and has no direction to report. Which basis a row uses is in its tooltip and in the stability table's curve_basis column. A feature whose row changes colour is not necessarily broken: it may genuinely matter differently in different years. But its mean effect is then a summary of disagreeing years, and the mean is the least informative number about it.

Historical settlement and bankroll

These are retrospective prices

Every figure in this section is settled against historical result-page odds and official dividends. Those are the prices after the pool closed, so no bet here could have been placed at them and nothing here establishes profitability.

Settled bankroll paths

Walk-forward fits
11
initial 2010-2015, expanding by one season per evaluation year
Boosting rounds
400
per seeded fit
Model members
5
seeded fits bagged
Evaluation
2016-2026
settled years shown
Rebate policy
10%
after a race loss reaches HK$10,000

Bankroll scenarios are solved independently because the rebate threshold is fixed in dollars; the larger bank is not a scaled copy of the smaller one. annual-reset re-settlement of continuous-path decisions: the same stakes, compounded from the declared opening balance at the start of each test year. Not an annual-reset sizing simulation -- stakes are not re-solved from reset capital, and doing so would change which bets are placed rather than only how they compound. Charts retain the extrema from up to 3,757 settled races; exact annual returns are computed from the full path before plotting is reduced. 2015 is excluded because its utility scale was not fitted.

Model-assumed simulation

Bankroll outcomes if model probabilities were true

Question answered: If the stored model probabilities were the true win probabilities, what range of cumulative Kelly returns and drawdowns could racing randomness produce at the observed odds?

Fixed stored context: published model view bagged_offset / historical Win Odds held fixed as the gross-return proxy / observed race chronology / evaluation years 2016-2026. Changing a control only reveals an already-computed trajectory; the browser performs no simulation or settlement arithmetic.
Controls shared with the other published reports
ControlValue
Simulation seed20,260,824
Replicates1,000
Races in the simulated population8,264
Races this model stakes2,053
Chart checkpoints355
Race-key population digestsha256:7df0a9491db9b6b1246c87c3d616ac79fd3f6d3354117317ef21cd1b72923b02
Kelly fractions1% Kelly, 2% Kelly, 5% Kelly, 10% Kelly
PoliciesRebate-aware Kelly, Kelly, no rebate

every race in the standardized evaluation window that the settlement can settle, not the subset this model staked. An unstaked race has multiplier exactly 1 under both policies, so including it changes no terminal figure; excluding it made the race sequence -- and with it the checkpoints and the shared random draws -- a property of the model, which is what stopped two reports' fan charts being comparable.

Every published report runs this simulation under these controls, so the same population digest and the same checkpoint count appear in every one. Only the row for races staked differs, and that difference is the model's own staking behaviour.

Model-assumed outcome simulation

Winners are drawn from the fitted probabilities. This isolates wagering variance conditional on the model being exactly right; it is not evidence that the estimated edge exists.

Rebate-aware large-bank limit

The rebate threshold is treated as always met. This is a scale-free asymptotic policy, not the exact finite HK$1B bankroll scenario. Minimum-bet rounding is omitted.

Assumptions:
  • Model probabilities are assumed exactly correct.
  • Historical Win Odds are held fixed and used as the gross return proxy.
  • Race opportunities and chronology are as observed.
  • Winners are drawn independently per race from the stored probabilities.
  • The model is not refitted inside a replicate.
  • Model error, drift, market response and regime change are excluded.

Metric definitions
Analytic expected return
Probability-weighted bankroll multipliers compounded through the observed race order.
Median terminal return
Half of simulated paths finish below this cumulative return and half above.
5th-percentile terminal return
Five percent of simulated paths finish at or below it.
Maximum drawdown
Largest peak-to-trough decline, including the opening bankroll as the initial peak.
Percentile bands
Exact cross-replicate quantiles at each stored chart checkpoint.
Model risk is not included

The model is not refitted inside a replicate. Probability error, model drift, market response and regime change are excluded, so these ranges describe outcome variation under the stored model and odds rather than uncertainty that the model will remain correct.

Limitations

Historical result-page odds are not executable prices

Every stake, return and bankroll figure in this report is computed against historical result-page odds and official dividends. Those are not an executable pre-race price: they are the prices after the pool closed, and a bet placed at them could not have been placed. Nothing here establishes profitability. A profitability claim requires a locked model shadow-tested against timestamped pre-race odds snapshots.

Every test year is also development data

Every year through 2026 has been used as development data in this repository: features were searched, architectures compared and thresholds inspected against these same seasons. The chronological split is real, so a test year is genuinely after its training rows, but no test year is unseen. Treat the forward figures as probability progress rather than as a locked out-of-sample result, and do not select a Kelly level or an edge threshold from this reused history. The confirmation step that this run cannot substitute for is a prospective shadow test against archived pre-race price snapshots.

What this report does not establish

  • It measures Softmax Offset against the market on the evaluated races. It is not a cross-model comparison, and nothing in it ranks this model against another published one.
  • The model-assumed simulation excludes model risk by construction. It answers what racing randomness could do if the stored probabilities were exactly right, so it is not evidence that the estimated edge exists.
  • No interval here bounds refit uncertainty, so no figure carries a stated range over the model itself -- a single number is not evidence of precision.
  • Every figure is out of sample in time but in sample in design: the feature set, the hyperparameters and the staking rules were all chosen with these years visible.
  • Nothing here is a shadow test. A profitability claim needs a locked model run forward against timestamped pre-race prices.

Known source-data defects

The lineage record carries {'landing_dataset': 'aspx-results', 'landing_duplicate_keys': 1513, 'landing_primary_key': ['race_id', 'Horse No.'], 'retained_key': ['race_id', 'Horse No.'], 'retained_policy': 'keep_first', 'retained_policy_source': 'features/build.py', 'feature_table_duplicate_keys': 0, 'absorbed_by_build': 1513, 'consistent': True}. Stated rather than corrected silently: the feature build absorbs these, and a reader auditing a number should know they exist.

How to verify this report

Provenance is not rendered in this document and it is not missing. Three files sit beside this one, and between them they carry everything the retired technical appendix printed:

FileWhat it lets a reader check
run_lock.jsonevery one of the 19 artifacts this report read, by content digest, with the lock digest of the run that produced them, the source commit and its clean-or-dirty state, and the model and config identity
manifest.jsonwhat this report wrote, by digest and byte size, with the rendering mode and the capability verdict for every section
summary.jsonthe model identity, the population identity, the headline metrics, the market-relationship metrics, every settled Kelly path's identity and endpoints, and the simulation policy inventory with its terminal metrics

This report was generated from source commit f9822340d03a, clean. Its metrics are measured on 8265 race keys whose digest is sha256:81e0285f5e0538d8a2293b4fd026ded45a23a454fbbc9204bdced2c90555728d. The published reports are compared on that digest before publication, so the claim that they cover the same races is checked rather than asserted.
